VZ.rationale: VZ screens as moderately attractive driven by a compelling valuation setup against a solid but unspectacular fundamental backdrop. The PE of 11.16x sits at the floor of its 365-day range (11.2x–21.2x), with the stock flat at ~$47 despite genuine earnings improvement — Q1 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.28 beat consensus by 5.8%, record EBITDA of $13.4B, and management raised full-year EPS guidance to $4.95–$4.99. The 9.0% earnings yield offers a ~460bp spread over the 10Y Treasury, and the ~5.9% dividend yield is supported by a ~55% payout ratio and $21.5B+ guided FCF. Franchise quality is solid: narrow-moat US wireless triopoly with 38% market share, 35–37% EBITDA margins, and structural FWA tailwinds cannibalizing cable broadband. However, the thesis is tempered by: (1) heavy leverage at D/E ~3.0x ($313B liabilities) with elevated rates (BAA 6.06%), (2) anemic revenue growth (+2.9% YoY, flat QoQ) making the margin expansion the sole earnings lever, (3) missing Q3/Q4 2025 data preventing full TTM confirmation of the trailing margin jump from 7.6% to 12.8%, and (4) competitive pressure from T-Mobile's broadband expansion. The near-term catalyst is the Q1 earnings beat and raised guidance, which has not yet been priced in — but the data gap and leverage risk prevent a higher conviction score. Score sits between mildly attractive (+0.2) and the conditional value case, reflecting a cheap stock on improving earnings with meaningful caveats on durability.
